## Observed deny text (consumer repro, Cursor Multitask parent)

**Implement-class `Task` spawn (`best-of-n-runner` and `generalPurpose`):**

```
Directive denied implement-class spawn: no worktree destination on the spawn payload (tool_input.isolation=worktree, Isolation, worktree_path, worktreePath, worktree, cwd, working_directory, workingDirectory, or workdir). Spawned mutating work takes its own worktree; do not inherit the parent checkout. Continue in the parent when the parent will do the writes -- exclusive of a live nursery occupancy grant on the same tree. Dest-placing is payload-root: Composer already on the reserved linked worktree (consult mints the reservation; do not pre-mint then Task), or dest-rooted @cursor/sdk Agent.create({ local: { cwd } }) after cursor-sdk-auth / CURSOR_API_KEY. A live nursery grant fences parent product writes in that tree. Spawn with assist / ephemeral markers for scratch. Use subagent_type explore when the spawn is actually a read-only spawn.
```

Passing `cwd`, `working_directory`, and `worktree_path` on the Task tool invocation did not clear this deny (fields may not be forwarded into the hook payload).

**Parent Write/Edit (same session, primary checkout):**

```
Directive denied Write: Occupancy is advisory coordination for accidental same-machine collision, not same-user authorization.
Worktree occupied by session host:claude:v1:… (intent=mutation, …).
This process presented session host:cursor:v1:…, which is this occupant's own host session under a second identity -- not a stranger.
Use another worktree. Do not steal this lease from yourself. Stay read-only (`session:start --read-only`) or isolate in a linked worktree and claim that tree.
```

**Read-only spawn (contrast):** `subagent_type: explore` with `run_in_background: true` was accepted; implement-class spawns were not.

## Dedup / triage note (evaluate + tip check)

**Validity:** still-open on tip. Not a duplicate of open or closed siblings.

**Related (keep open / cite):**
- #4294 — complementary Cursor carve-out for `tool_input.environment=cloud` (skip local dest consult). Different MVP from this ticket's local `best-of-n-runner` auto-worktree registry.
- #3613 — occupancy-model tracker; useful parent for the stretch dual-identity limb (`host:cursor:…` vs `host:claude:…` on the same `payloadRoot`).
- Closed context (shipped dest-placing / recovery copy, not this residual): #4295, #4362, #4321.

**Workaround vs blocker:** **Workaround exists** → labeled `urgent`, not `adoption-blocker`.

Documented Cursor hatches that unblock implement without Cursor Task dest fields (see `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/host-cursor.md`):
1. **Nursery inherit** — open Composer already on the reserved linked worktree; one Task child may inherit that payload root.
2. **Dest-rooted SDK** — `@cursor/sdk` `Agent.create({ local: { cwd: <reserved-worktree> } })` after `cursor-sdk-auth` / `CURSOR_API_KEY`.
3. Optional adjacent path once #4294 lands: cloud `environment: "cloud"` (isolation is host VM, not local dest proof).

Occupancy dual-identity lockout: tip already classifies cursor-vs-claude as own-host under a second identity and steers to another worktree / read-only / release+reclaim — friction, not a no-path hard stop.

**Non-goal of this note:** do not weaken fail-closed dest policy for unmarked `generalPurpose` on primary.

## In plain English

Cursor Multitask parents on the primary checkout cannot pass Task dest fields, so implement-class Task (including best-of-n-runner) is denied as dest-missing. Tip already has two real hatches: open Composer on a linked worktree (nursery inherit) or dest-rooted @cursor/sdk. Auto-allowing best-of-n from a primary window without a proven child worktree would either mutate primary (issue non-goal) or trust Cursor isolation the hook cannot see. Prefer-A ships the spawn matrix + Multitask parent read-only posture + clearer deny copy naming subagent_type, locks nursery/SDK for best-of-n when the window is already dest-rooted, and parks primary-window auto-worktree registry until a measured payload signal proves isolation.

## Lean

Bind Approach A.

### Approach A (Prefer)

1. Publish a Cursor payload-host spawn matrix in host-cursor.md (explore / best-of-n-runner / generalPurpose / nursery inherit / dest-rooted SDK / cloud #4294) with a short pointer from commands.md or CURSOR_TASK_SPAWN_CLASS_RECOVERY.
2. Rewrite Cursor Task dest-missing deny to name the presented subagent_type and point at that matrix; keep nursery/SDK as the implement hatches; do not advertise stripped Task dest keys as the recovery.
3. Document Multitask parent on primary as read-only coordinator (explore OK); mutation lease lives on the linked child worktree via nursery or SDK.
4. Regression-lock: nursery inherit already admits implement-class Task (including best-of-n-runner) when payload root is a non-primary linked worktree — add an explicit fixture so best-of-n is not treated as a special deny.
5. Dual-identity (cursor vs claude on same payloadRoot): keep fail-closed own-host second-identity steer; tighten recovery copy toward session:ready from project root / linked-worktree claim / read-only; stretch same-operator soft-pass deferred as leftover citing #3613 unless a thin tip-local copy-only limb lands in-file_scope.
6. Remint AC1: passing PreToolUse for best-of-n+implement means nursery or SDK child-worktree path under clean ritual/lease — not primary-window auto-allow.

### Approach B

Primary-window auto-worktree registry: when subagent_type is in a documented set (min best-of-n-runner), skip dest-missing and allow implement-class spawn from primary Multitask parent, trusting Cursor to isolate. Reject as Prefer-A: tip cannot re-root Task (updated_input dest fields do not move the child); host-cursor already forbids sequencing best-of-n ahead of nursery; issue non-goal forbids primary mutation without isolation; hook has no measured isolation signal today.

### Approach C

Soft-pass occupancy when host:cursor and host:claude are the same human on the same payloadRoot so Multitask parent Write proceeds after terminal session:ready. Reject as co-equal v1 Prefer-A limb: occupancy identity remains the collision fence (#3613); stretch only as leftover UX/docs, not a lease merge.

## Reject

- Allow implement-class Task from primary Multitask window for best-of-n (or any registry) without nursery/SDK or a measured child-isolation payload signal.
- Require Cursor to add cwd/worktree_path Task fields.
- Weaken fail-closed dest policy for unmarked generalPurpose on primary.
- Unpark fence-in-place as a co-equal v1 limb.
- Treat #4294 cloud carve-out as the local MVP.

## file_scope (lean)

- content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/host-cursor.md
- packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts (CURSOR_TASK_SPAWN_* recovery / deny overlay)
- packages/core/src/session/spawn-occupancy.ts (only if nursery best-of-n fixture needs a named allow path comment/helper — prefer test-only if tip already admits)
- packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher-spawn-dest.test.ts / spawn-occupancy.test.ts
- content/commands.md (short matrix pointer) if recovery cannot carry the link alone
- CHANGELOG.md

## Keep-outs

- #4294 cloud environment carve-out product
- #3613 full occupancy-model redesign (leftover cite for stretch soft-pass)
- Fence-in-place (#4295 parked)
- Grok spawn_subagent plan skip / non-Cursor hosts

Round 1, fresh Codex seat. Reviewed Prefer-A 6269945684 and Stop 1 6269952260, observed-deny 6269596818, triage 6269850079, and panel-deposit 6270034785. Inclusive ceiling: 6270034785; no sibling critic input. Pin-read source and existing tests at bc682707737c3f7ff5acb4d98d87c1b140b54ee6; no runtime Cursor experiment or test execution.

**Assessment:** Approach A is a defensible narrower delivery. No blocks-the-design finding on retaining the current fail-closed policy. It does not fix native implement Task dispatch from a primary Multitask window, and SDK success cannot establish native Task success.

Existing mechanisms: [spawn-occupancy.ts](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/bc682707737c3f7ff5acb4d98d87c1b140b54ee6/packages/core/src/session/spawn-occupancy.ts) calls consultCursorNurseryInherit before destination-missing for Cursor without a destination. It verifies a non-primary linked worktree, rejects an occupant other than parentId, and rejects an existing dispatch reservation. This is not a best-of-n allowlist. [Existing nursery tests](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/bc682707737c3f7ff5acb4d98d87c1b140b54ee6/packages/core/src/session/spawn-occupancy.test.ts) already cover generalPurpose admission, primary denial, second-Task conflict, child grant and parent fencing. [host-cursor.md](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/bc682707737c3f7ff5acb4d98d87c1b140b54ee6/content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/host-cursor.md) documents nursery first, dest-rooted SDK second, stripped Task destination keys, and the best-of-n sequencing keep-out. [dispatcher.ts](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/bc682707737c3f7ff5acb4d98d87c1b140b54ee6/packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts) already overlays Cursor-specific recovery, including explore-only read-only guidance and no Cursor plan exemption.

1. **sharpens-framing — Remint AC1 as two separate checks, not “nursery or SDK.”** Evidence: the issue AC1 names native Task + best-of-n-runner; draft item 6 allows nursery or SDK, while host-cursor describes SDK as a separate session whose leaf does not nested-Task. Failure mode: an SDK launch passes acceptance while the named native Task case remains unverified. Consequence: keep native Task/best-of-n admission in a dest-rooted nursery as the specific regression criterion; document SDK independently. A fixture proves Directive's decision for the supplied payload, not that actual best-of-n execution retains that payload root or its worktree identity. Label that host-behavior boundary explicitly.

2. **sharpens-framing — Preserve the original primary-window residual in the scope statement.** Evidence: draft item 6 openly remints AC1, and the pinned nursery test still expects destination-missing on primary. The issue's expected-behavior section requests registry-based primary-window admission, even though its AC1 already mentions a child worktree. Failure mode: shipping documentation plus an existing-path regression is reported as delivering the requested auto-worktree capability. Consequence: Approach A may bind as the narrowed matrix/recovery/regression slice, but state that primary-window native implement Task remains unsupported and give the parked capability an explicit disposition. The remint is honest in the draft; preserve that honesty in the eventual delivery claim rather than describing all of the original request as resolved.

3. **sharpens-framing — Make occupancy recovery depend on the presented identity, not merely “session:ready from project root.”** Evidence: observed-deny records terminal host:claude versus chat host:cursor; consultCursorNurseryInherit rejects any live occupant unequal to parentId, even on a linked worktree. Failure mode: the operator repeats terminal session:ready in the recommended child tree, recreates the mismatched lease, and nursery still refuses. Consequence: the matrix must distinguish destination-missing, destination-occupied and ritual failure; retain the existing own-host second-identity steer and state that a clean nursery lease must match the actual Cursor parent identity. Do not present a root-directory correction as an identity repair. Keep same-human lease merging outside this slice.

4. **sharpens-framing — Spell out nursery cardinality and parent location in the Multitask pattern.** Evidence: host-cursor and the existing tests admit one child per nursery window and fence that window's parent product writes; a second Task reservation conflicts. Failure mode: “primary parent read-only, child worktree mutation” is read as permission for the primary window to fan out native implement Tasks, or for several workers to share one nursery. Consequence: show the actual transition: primary coordination stays read-only; native Task requires Composer already rooted in its linked nursery, with one live reservation; SDK is the separate dest-rooted launch alternative. Include second-child refusal and parent-write fencing alongside the new best-of-n positive fixture.

5. **footnote — A measured registry remains a plausible later design, but a type-name allowlist alone is not the missing proof.** Its strongest case is that Cursor already guarantees isolation for best-of-n, so Directive could recognize that host contract without new Task fields. The supplied envelope contains the reported guarantee, not a measured binding from this pre-spawn request to a concrete isolated child. A trustworthy host isolation contract plus evidence of child-root binding, reservation/lease handling and concurrent-worker separation would change my verdict; a prompt assertion, stripped destination key or subagent_type string alone would not. Parking this limb is justified for Approach A, without declaring it impossible.

Injection/swarm assessment: preserve the separation between agent-supplied task labels and host-established destination/identity. The reviewed design adds no reason to promote prompt text into isolation authority, merge host:cursor and host:claude leases, or bypass foreign-occupant/second-reservation refusal. When displaying the presented subagent_type in recovery, render it as bounded diagnostic data. Keep primary-window denial, cross-identity refusal and nursery parent fencing in the regression boundary. No new registry or occupancy soft-pass is needed to ship the narrowed slice.

## Round-1 critic — open critique of Prefer-A 6269945684 / Stop 1 6269952260

Verification: pin-read `git show bc682707737c3f7ff5acb4d98d87c1b140b54ee6:` on `packages/core/src/session/spawn-occupancy.ts`, `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts`, `packages/core/src/hooks/readonly.ts`, `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/host-cursor.md`. No mutation, no ingest.

### Inventory first (what tip already has)

- `consultCursorNurseryInherit` (spawn-occupancy.ts:407) admits implement-class Cursor Task when `payloadRoot` is a non-primary linked worktree, with no live foreign occupant and no existing reservation. It never inspects `subagent_type`.
- `applyCursorNurseryOccupancy` (spawn-occupancy.ts:1015) grants the child and then denies the *parent's* product writes in that tree (`NURSERY_PARENT_WRITE_DENY`, :1004).
- `subagent_type` is already a live classifier key on Cursor: `explore` -> read-only admit (readonly.ts:121-126; 6269596818 confirms explore was accepted on this host), `{ephemeral,docs,assist}` -> implementation-gate skip (readonly.ts:242-268). `isProcessOnlyCriticSpawn` (readonly.ts:373) is Grok-`spawn_subagent`-gated and never reaches Cursor.
- `git grep -n best-of-n-runner` over `packages/core/src` at the dispatch SHA: **zero hits**.
- Dest-missing copy is minted by `rerootMissingDestMessage()` (spawn-occupancy.ts:309); `overlayCursorTaskSpawnRecovery` (dispatcher.ts, replace at :493) is a pure string swap over `(host, toolName, decision)`.

---

### 1. blocks-the-design — limb 3's documented pattern is unreachable by the mechanism it names

Limb 3 documents "Multitask parent on primary as read-only coordinator; mutation lease lives on the linked child worktree **via nursery** or SDK."

Evidence: `consultCursorNurseryInherit` returns `null` unless `isLinkedWorktreePath(payloadRoot)` and `!isMainWorktreePath(payloadRoot)` (spawn-occupancy.ts:412-414); `applyCursorNurseryOccupancy` short-circuits unless `isCursorNurseryDest(dest)` holds those same two predicates. A parent window rooted on primary can never reach the nursery branch at :531 — it falls straight through to the `destination-missing` deny at :541.

Failure mode: an operator reads the published matrix, keeps the Multitask parent on primary, fires `best-of-n-runner`, and gets the identical deny recorded in 6269596818. The one realizable nursery posture is the inverse of what limb 3 writes down: the parent window **is** the linked worktree, and while its single child runs that parent is fenced out of writing in its own tree (`NURSERY_PARENT_WRITE_DENY`).

Disposition consequence: limb 3 and its matrix row must split into two postures — (a) parent-on-worktree nursery, parent write-fenced, one child, second Task is reservation-conflict; (b) parent-on-primary, mutation only via dest-rooted SDK. Shipping them as one "parent RO on primary + nursery child" row publishes a path that cannot execute.

### 2. blocks-the-design — AC1 as reminted is already green at the dispatch SHA, and no P1 leftover is recorded

Limb 6 remints AC1 to "nursery or SDK child-worktree path under clean ritual/lease". Under that reading AC1 already holds at bc68270: nursery admits implement-class Task irrespective of `subagent_type`, and `best-of-n-runner` appears nowhere in `packages/core/src`. Limb 4's "regression-lock so best-of-n is not treated as a special deny" therefore locks the absence of a special case that was never written — a legitimate fixture, but zero behavior delta.

Failure mode: Approach A as drafted relieves the copy and matrix pain and relieves **none** of the primary-window spawn pain. The reported repro — primary-window Multitask parent, implement Task — denies exactly as before. The only recorded leftover is the dual-identity stretch to #3613; the parked registry limb carries no leftover cite, so the primary-window item reads as relieved by limbs 4+6 when it has in fact been reclassified as working-as-intended.

Disposition consequence: the lean cannot bind honestly without (i) naming AC1-as-reminted an already-holding invariant rather than a deliverable, and (ii) an explicit leftover for the primary-window auto-worktree item with its own cite. The remint also drops the issue's Expected-behavior section 1, which is unambiguously about the primary window — reminting AC1's sentence does not dispose of that section.
